messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@helixops.com>

Cc: HelixOps Contracts <contracts@helixops.com>, Ben Foster <ben.foster@helixops.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixOps redlines on MSA/DPA + SOW (attached)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the integration surface between HelixOps and Redwood. We've run our legal review and attached redlines for the MSA and DPA, plus an updated SOW with the initial deliverables and milestones. A few high-level asks from our side: 

- Increase the liability cap to 3x fees for gross negligence and data incidents (current cap looks lower).
- Audit and on-site inspection clause: we need a more explicit right to audit security controls annually (third-party SOC2 assessments are OK, but we want an indemnified on-site right).
- Subprocessor list: please provide an initial list or an approved-subprocessor process rather than case-by-case consent.
- Data residency: require EU-only processing for EU customer data in the DPA (we can provide a Def-Region list).
- SOW: tighten the acceptance criteria for the connector deliverables and add a 30-day warranty window post-acceptance.

I've attached the marked-up documents (HelixOps_MSA_redlines_v1.docx, HelixOps_SOW_v2.pdf). Can your team review and come back with a consolidated position? We're hoping to close legal by the end of next week to hit our Q4 joint launch.

Best,
Emily
Emily Carter
Head of Partnerships, HelixOps
https://helixops.com

Subject: Re: HelixOps redlines on MSA/DPA + SOW (attached)

Naomi / team — I reviewed the redlines and drafted responses inline. High-level positions below (will send a marked-up MSA/DPA back as a follow-up):

1) Liability cap: we can consider 3x fees but limited to incidents attributable to our gross negligence or willful misconduct. For data breaches we can propose a carve-out for statutory liabilities (where applicable). Commercial should be prepared to offset via a one-time integration fee or reduced onboarding credits.

2) Audit rights: we won't agree to unrestricted on-site audits. Proposed compromise: annual third-party SOC2 Type II report to be shared within 30 days of request plus a mutually agreeable, limited on-site audit right triggered only by a material security incident and with reasonable notice and scope limitations.

3) Subprocessors: provide an initial list of subprocessors and a notice-and-approval mechanism limited to changes that materially affect data flow. We use an approved-subprocessor process (notify + objection window) — that's standard for our customers and partners.

4) Data residency: we cannot commit to EU-only processing for all EU customer data on our hosted tier unless they opt into a Dedicated/Private deployment. We can offer contract language requiring processing within EU regions for EU customer environments (if HelixOps requires EU-only processing as a mandatory term we should flag Dedicated deployment as the solution).

5) SOW acceptance & warranty: accept the 30-day warranty request but propose using a joint acceptance certificate template and a 10-business-day remediation window prior to formal rejection. That should be acceptable if implementation acceptance criteria are clearly defined.

I'll attach a redline shortly. Sergio — if commercial wants to propose a fee trade or extended warranty instead of raising cap, flag what you think is feasible.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Laura, Naomi — appreciate the quick review. A few clarifications from Contracts team: 

- On the audit point, HelixOps' standard is to retain a contractual right to one annual audit by a certified third party or, if necessary, an on-site review limited to the connector infrastructure. We can agree to reasonable scope limits.
- For subprocessor notification, we'd accept an approved-subprocessor model but we'd prefer an approval window rather than a pure notice model.
- Regarding data residency: HelixOps' customers include EU-headquartered enterprises who require EU-only processing in contract. If Redwood cannot commit at the MSA level, this will force us to require dedicated deployments with associated commercial implications.

Can Redwood provide an example list of current subprocessors and a proposed clause for subprocessor objections? Also please advise on expected commercial impact if we must move to Dedicated for EU-only customers.

Thanks,
HelixOps Contracts
contracts@helixops.com

Subject: Re: HelixOps redlines on MSA/DPA + SOW (attached)

Hi everyone — commercial perspective and proposed tradeoffs: 

1) Liability cap: Redwood can accept an uplift to a 3x fees cap for data incidents if HelixOps agrees to (a) a modest onboarding fee of $30k to cover integration QA and (b) a 12-month minimum committed usage (we can do this as a credit schedule in the SOW).

2) Dedicated deployments for EU customers: moving to Dedicated has a material cost (our pricing model for Dedicated includes reserved GPU capacity and support). If HelixOps requires EU-only processing for a customer, we can provide a Dedicated option and outline the delta in a separate schedule; we can also provide a transitional commitment for hosted while the customer onboards to Dedicated over 60 days.

3) Subprocessor list: attaching our current subprocessors list and a proposed approval window clause: notify + 10 business day objection (for material changes).

If this is acceptable, Naomi — let's finalize commitments and I can put the financials into the draft SOW. Emily — are you able to circulate a projected customer profile (how many EU-only customers you expect in the first year)? That will help us size Dedicated capacity.

Thanks,
